title: Eventual flatness for finitely presented modules over affine inverse limits
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and let $(R_j)_{j\in I}$ be a directed system of rings with colimit $R$. Fix $i\in I$, and let $A_i\to B_i$ be a map of finitely presented $R_i$-algebras. Let $N_i$ be a finitely presented $B_i$-module. For $j\ge i$ set $A_j=R_j\otimes_{R_i}A_i$, $B_j=R_j\otimes_{R_i}B_i$, and $N_j=R_j\otimes_{R_i}N_i$; set $A=R\otimes_{R_i}A_i$, $B=R\otimes_{R_i}B_i$, and $N=R\otimes_{R_i}N_i$. If $N$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then there exists $j_0\ge i$ such that $N_j$ is flat over $A_j$ for every $j\ge j_0$. (No Noetherian hypothesis is needed.)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the given systems; finite presentation; Noetherian approximation).* $A_i$ is of finite type over $R_i$ (being of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]) and $B_i$ is of finite presentation over $R_i$, so $A_i\to B_i$ is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-over-finite-type-algebra]. By associativity of $\otimes$, $B=R\otimes_{R_i}B_i\cong A\otimes_{A_i}B_i$ and $B_j\cong A_j\otimes_{A_i}B_i$ as algebras, under which $A\to B$, $A_j\to B_j$ become $a\mapsto a\otimes1$; so $A\to B$ and every $A_j\to B_j$ are of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] (1), and $B_k\cong A_k\otimes_{A_j}B_j$ for $i\le j\le k$ (also with $A,B$ in place of $A_k,B_k$). Likewise $N\cong B\otimes_{B_i}N_i$ and $N_j\cong B_j\otimes_{B_i}N_i$, finitely presented over $B$, resp. $B_j$, by [lem-pc-fp-module-base-change], and $N_k\cong B_k\otimes_{B_j}N_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise] (with $M_0=A_i$, $B_i$, resp. $N_i$ over the system $(R_j)_{j\ge i}$) and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion], $A$, $B$, $N$ are the colimits of the abelian groups $A_j$, $B_j$, $N_j$; for a cocone of ring maps the induced additive map is multiplicative and unital, any two elements coming from one stage, $A=\varinjlim A_j$ and $B=\varinjlim B_j$ as rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and $N=\varinjlim N_j$ compatibly with the module structures. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation] to $A\to B$ and $N$ (its $R\to S$, $M$): a nonempty directed set $(\Lambda,\le)$, ring maps $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$, $S_\lambda$-modules $M_\lambda$, with $A=\varinjlim R_\lambda$, $B=\varinjlim S_\lambda$, $N=\varinjlim M_\lambda$ and its clauses (1)-(4). $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian (every ideal is principal), so each $R_\lambda$ (finite type over $\mathbf Z$) and each $S_\lambda$ (finite type over $R_\lambda$) is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and $S_\lambda$ is of finite presentation over $R_\lambda$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]; $M_\lambda$, finite over the Noetherian $S_\lambda$, is finitely presented [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation]. Throughout, $R_\lambda,S_\lambda,M_\lambda$ denote this approximation and $A_j,B_j,N_j$ the prescribed system; for a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ write $\mathfrak p$ for its inverse image in $A$ and $\mathfrak q_\lambda\subset S_\lambda$, $\mathfrak p_\lambda\subset R_\lambda$ for its inverse images.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.168.1, Tag 02JO, proof of (3), first paragraph

proof.text: Fix a prime q of B, with p its inverse image in A, and localize the approximation at q_λ and p_λ. The localization-colimit lemma gives colimits A_p=colim (R_λ)_{p_λ} and B_q=colim (S_λ)_{q_λ}, with local transition maps. These localized rings are Noetherian local rings; the induced map is local. Localization-tensor lemmas give the localization condition (a) for (S_λ)_{q_λ}⊗_{(R_λ)_{p_λ}}(R_μ)_{p_μ}\to (S_μ)_{q_μ}, and the transition isomorphism for localized modules gives condition (b), (M_λ)_{q_λ}⊗_{(S_λ)_{q_λ}}(S_μ)_{q_μ}≅(M_μ)_{q_μ}. The colimit module is N_q: this follows by writing (M_λ)_{q_λ}≅M_λ⊗_{S_λ}(S_λ)_{q_λ}, applying localization-tensor-over-base, and commuting tensor with the filtered colimit B_q=colim (S_λ)_{q_λ}; the filtered-colimit module criterion then identifies the result. It is flat over A_p because N is flat over A and the only-if direction of the prime-local flatness criterion applies.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.168.1, Tag 02JO, proof of (1), first paragraph

proof.text: The hypotheses just checked allow the local eventual-flatness lemma to be applied to the localized systems, so for this q there is λ(q) such that (M_λ(q))_{q_λ(q)} is flat over (R_λ(q))_{p_λ(q)}.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.168.1, Tag 02JO, proof of (1), first paragraph

proof.text: *Step 4 (the flat loci $U_\lambda$; persistence).* For $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let $U_\lambda=\{\mathfrak q'\in\operatorname{Spec}S_\lambda:(M_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q'}\text{ is a flat }R_\lambda\text{-module}\}$; it is open by [lem-weil-pbc-openness-of-flatness] ($R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$ and $M_\lambda$ of finite presentation, step 1). Claim: if $\lambda\le\mu$ and $\mathfrak q'\in\operatorname{Spec}S_\mu$ has inverse image $\mathfrak q''\in U_\lambda$, then $\mathfrak q'\in U_\mu$. Proof: let $T=S_\lambda\setminus\mathfrak q''$ and $\mathfrak p'$ the inverse image of $\mathfrak q'$ in $R_\mu$. By clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation] and associativity, $M_\mu\cong M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu\cong M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}(S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu)\cong M_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu$ as $S_\mu$-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (its $R=R_\lambda$, $A=S_\lambda$, $M=M_\lambda$, $N=R_\mu$) the localization $P=T^{-1}M_\mu$ at the image of $T$ is $(M_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q''}\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu$, a flat $R_\mu$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] since $(M_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q''}$ is $R_\lambda$-flat. $P$ is an $S_\mu$-module, so by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-local-criterion] (for $R_\mu\to S_\mu$ and $P$) $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a flat $(R_\mu)_{\mathfrak p'}$-module. The image of $T$ lies in $S_\mu\setminus\mathfrak q'$, so $P_{\mathfrak q'}=(M_\mu)_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] (the conditions of a localization are checked directly), and since it is an $(R_\mu)_{\mathfrak p'}$-module, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] makes it a flat $R_\mu$-module: $\mathfrak q'\in U_\mu$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.168.1, Tag 02JO, proof of (1), second paragraph

proof.text: *Step 5 (quasi-compactness).* For a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$, step 3 gives $\lambda(\mathfrak q)$ with $(M_{\lambda(\mathfrak q)})_{\mathfrak q_{\lambda(\mathfrak q)}}$ flat over $(R_{\lambda(\mathfrak q)})_{\mathfrak p_{\lambda(\mathfrak q)}}$; it is a module over that localization (elements of $R_\lambda\setminus\mathfrak p_\lambda$ map outside $\mathfrak q_\lambda$), so it is flat over $R_{\lambda(\mathfrak q)}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization], i.e. $\mathfrak q_{\lambda(\mathfrak q)}\in U_{\lambda(\mathfrak q)}$, and by step 4 $\mathfrak q_\mu\in U_\mu$ for all $\mu\ge\lambda(\mathfrak q)$ ($\mathfrak q_\lambda$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak q_\mu$). Let $V_\lambda\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$ be the inverse image of $U_\lambda$, open (the preimage of $V(J)$ is $V(JB)$). Step 4 gives $V_\lambda\subseteq V_\mu$ for $\lambda\le\mu$, and the above gives $\bigcup_\lambda V_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}B$. $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (iii), so finitely many $V_\lambda$ cover it; $\Lambda$ being directed there is $\lambda_0$ above their indices, and $V_{\lambda_0}=\operatorname{Spec}B$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.168.1, Tag 02JO, proof of (1), second paragraph

proof.text: *Step 6 (a stage with full flat locus).* Write $\operatorname{Spec}S_{\lambda_0}\setminus U_{\lambda_0}=V(J)$, $J\subseteq S_{\lambda_0}$ an ideal. Since $V_{\lambda_0}=\operatorname{Spec}B$, no prime of $B$ contains the image of $J$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (i) the images of the elements of $J$ generate the unit ideal of $B$: $1=\sum_{k=1}^r\bar f_kb_k$ with $f_k\in J$, $b_k\in B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (2) ($R=\mathbf Z$) and directedness the $b_k$ come from some $S_{\lambda}$, $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero] the relation holds in some $S_{\lambda_1}$, $\lambda_1\ge\lambda$. Every prime of $S_{\lambda_1}$ avoids some $\bar f_k$, so its inverse image in $S_{\lambda_0}$ lies in $U_{\lambda_0}$, and by step 4 it lies in $U_{\lambda_1}$: $U_{\lambda_1}=\operatorname{Spec}S_{\lambda_1}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.168.1, Tag 02JO, proof of (1), third paragraph

proof.text: *Step 7 (a flat Noetherian model).* Put $R'=R_{\lambda_1}$, $S'=S_{\lambda_1}$, $M'=M_{\lambda_1}$. For every prime $\mathfrak q'$ of $S'$, with inverse image $\mathfrak p'$ in $R'$, $(M')_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a flat $R'$-module (step 6) and an $R'_{\mathfrak p'}$-module, hence a flat $R'_{\mathfrak p'}$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization]. By [lem-pc-affine-sections-flat-over-base] (its $A=R'$, $B=S'$, $M=M'$), $M'$ is a flat $R'$-module.

*Step 8 (the model reaches the prescribed system).* $R'$ is of finite presentation over $\mathbf Z$ and $S'$ over $R'$ (step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] (base $\mathbf Z$, the system $(A_j)_{j\ge i}$ with colimit $A$, step 1) the coprojection $R'	o A$ factors through some $A_{j_1}$; for $j\ge j_1$ regard $A_j$ and $B_j$ as $R'$-algebras through it. Then $(B_j)_{j\ge j_1}$ is a system of $R'$-algebras with colimit $B$ (step 1) and $R'$-algebra coprojections, and the coprojection $S'	o B$ is an $R'$-algebra map (clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation]); the same node over $R'$ gives $j_2\ge j_1$ and an $R'$-algebra map $\sigma:S'	o B_{j_2}$ through which $S'	o B$ factors. Put $D=S'\otimes_{R'}A_{j_2}$, finitely presented over $A_{j_2}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] (1), and $\Psi:D	o B_{j_2}$, $s\otimes a\mapsto\sigma(s)a$, a map of $A_{j_2}$-algebras; $B_{j_2}$ is finitely presented over $A_{j_2}$ (step 1). After $-\otimes_{A_{j_2}}A$, $D\otimes_{A_{j_2}}A=S'\otimes_{R'}A$ and $B_{j_2}\otimes_{A_{j_2}}A\cong B$ (step 1), and $\Psi\otimes1_A$ is the canonical map $S'\otimes_{R'}A	o B$, an isomorphism by clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation]. By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-category-fp-algebras] (2) (system $(A_j)_{j\ge j_2}$, colimit $A$) applied to $(\Psi\otimes1_A)^{-1}$ there are $\mu\ge j_2$ and $\chi:B_{j_2}\otimes_{A_{j_2}}A_\mu	o D\otimes_{A_{j_2}}A_\mu$ with $\chi\otimes1_A=(\Psi\otimes1_A)^{-1}$; by its (3), applied to $\chi\circ(\Psi\otimes1_{A_\mu})$ and the identity and to $(\Psi\otimes1_{A_\mu})\circ\chi$ and the identity, there is $

proof.text: *Step 9 (conclusion).* $M'$ is a flat $R'$-module (step 7), so $M'\otimes_{R'}A_j$ is a flat $A_j$-module for every $j\ge j_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]; by step 8, $N_j\cong M'\otimes_{R'}A_j$ as $A_j$-modules, so $N_j$ is flat over $A_j$ for every $j\ge j_0$.

split_report.summary: Repaired the Tag 02JO(3) proof in nine steps. The Noetherian approximation is localized with every hypothesis of the local eventual-flatness lemma checked; openness, persistence, quasi-compactness, and the unit-ideal argument produce one flat finite-type stage; finite-presentation algebra and module descent then compare that stage with the prescribed tensor system and base change gives all later flat modules.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the ancestor Noetherian-approximation step for eventual flatness of a finitely presented module (Tag 02JO(3)), including the localized prime argument and final comparison with the prescribed stages.

tool_uses.why: The proof uses the general finite-presentation approximation construction as a tool outside this unit.
The proof uses the local algebra eventual-flatness criterion as a tool for the localized systems.
The proof uses the general openness theorem for flat loci to obtain a finite affine cover.
The proof uses finite-presentation morphism descent to compare the Noetherian model algebra with prescribed stages.
The proof uses elementwise colimit/base-change facts to form the prescribed comparison maps.
The proof uses the general localization-of-filtered-colimit construction for the prime-local systems.
The proof uses the underlying-module colimit statement to identify the localized module colimit.

lean.statement: theorem exists_eventually_flat_of_finitePresentation {I : Type v} [Preorder I] [IsDirectedOrder I] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{v}) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c) {i : I} {Ai Bi Ni : Type w} [CommRing Ai] [CommRing Bi] [AddCommMonoid Ni] [Algebra (F.obj i : Type v) Ai] [Algebra (F.obj i : Type v) Bi] [Module Bi Ni] [Module.FinitePresentation Bi Ni] [Algebra.FinitePresentation (F.obj i : Type v) Ai] [Algebra.FinitePresentation (F.obj i : Type v) Bi] (f : Ai →ₐ[(F.obj i : Type v)] Bi) (hflat : letI : Module Ai Ni := Module.compHom Ni f.toRingHom letI : Algebra (F.obj i : Type v) (c.pt : Type v) := (c.ι.app i).hom.toAlgebra letI : Algebra Ai ((c.pt : Type v) ⊗[(F.obj i : Type v)] Ai) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra Module.Flat ((c.pt : Type v) ⊗[(F.obj i : Type v)] Ai) (((c.pt : Type v) ⊗[(F.obj i : Type v)] Ai) ⊗[Ai] Ni)) : (letI : Module Ai Ni := Module.compHom Ni f.toRingHom; ∃ j₀ : I, i ≤ j₀ ∧ ∀ (j : I) (h₀ : i ≤ j₀) (h₁ : j₀ ≤ j), (letI : Algebra (F.obj i : Type v) (F.obj j : Type v) := (F.map (homOfLE (h₀.trans h₁))).hom.toAlgebra; letI : Algebra Ai ((F.obj j : Type v) ⊗[(F.obj i : Type v)] Ai) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra; Module.Flat ((F.obj j : Type v) ⊗[(F.obj i : Type v)] Ai) (((F.obj j : Type v) ⊗[(F.obj i : Type v)] Ai) ⊗[Ai] Ni)))
